claims.text: NbTaTiV is an equiatomic BCC high-entropy alloy suitable as the baseline system.
Partially substituting Ta with the larger-radius elements Hf or Zr will systematically increase lattice misfit.
Increasing lattice misfit will hinder screw-dislocation glide.
Increasing lattice misfit will promote a shift toward edge-dislocation-dominated deformation.
The dislocation-mechanism shift will enhance solid-solution strengthening, hardness, and yield strength up to a critical misfit.
Beyond a critical misfit, phase instability or competing mechanisms may cause strengthening to plateau or reverse.
The effect of lattice misfit can be decoupled from other compositional influences using diffraction and atomistic simulation.
A misfit below approximately 5–7% defines a compositional window that maintains BCC phase stability.
Diffraction and simulation metrics can quantify the intensity of lattice distortion.
TEM can directly distinguish screw and edge dislocation character in the proposed samples.
Local lattice distortions induced by increased misfit impede screw-dislocation motion.
Edge dislocations are more strongly pinned by the induced lattice irregularities.
Stronger pinning increases obstacle resistance to dislocation motion and consequently increases hardness and yield strength.
Within the BCC stability window, higher-misfit samples will have greater hardness than the unsubstituted baseline.
Within the BCC stability window, higher-misfit samples will have greater yield strength than the unsubstituted baseline.
The unsubstituted equiatomic NbTaTiV baseline has minimal lattice misfit.
The proposed mechanism is limited to room-temperature testing at controlled strain rates and compositions retaining BCC stability.
Absence of either the screw-to-edge shift or the predicted strengthening relative to baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The plateau or reversal is framed as a possible consequence beyond the critical misfit, potentially outside the stated BCC-stability boundary, but failure to observe that optional out-of-boundary trend is nevertheless declared falsifying.

The design calls the substituted series equiatomic even though replacing only a fraction of the original 25 at.% Ta with Hf or Zr generally produces a non-equiatomic multicomponent composition unless all elemental fractions are rebalanced.
